turns.doctor_question: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, nice to meet you too. Um, I came in because... well, ever since I tried to turn my art into an actual freelance business, I've just been having a really hard time. 

I keep getting so wound up over things like invoices and client messages. I get overwhelmed and then I just avoid them completely... until I end up crying at my kitchen table, or I realize I'm forgetting normal stuff, like paying my own bills. It's just gotten to be a bit too much to handle on my own.

symptom_reasoning.S081: The patient describes developing overwhelming emotional distress, avoidance, crying, and functional disruption directly in response to an identifiable stressor (launching a freelance art business).

turns.doctor_question: Have you been having sudden attacks of intense fear or panic that come on out of the blue?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. I don't think I've had anything like that. It's never really out of the blue. It's pretty much always tied to the business... like, I'll get really stressed and overwhelmed when I have to deal with my inbox or money stuff, but I haven't had any sudden panic attacks for no reason.

turns.doctor_question: Did these problems start after you began trying to make your art into a freelance business?
turns.patient_response: Yes, they did. I'd say I started getting this overwhelmed and avoidant about a month after I took on a community arts contract. That was when I really tried to make the business more formal, and that's when all this started.

symptom_reasoning.S081: The patient confirms that their symptoms of feeling overwhelmed and avoidant began about a month after taking on a community arts contract and formalizing their business, demonstrating an emotional/behavioral response to an identifiable stressor.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been losing interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
turns.patient_response: No, I wouldn't say that. I still enjoy the things I usually like doing. Um, even my art is still fun when I'm just making it for myself and not worrying about a contract. It's really just the business side of things that makes me feel so overwhelmed. I still like doing my normal hobbies and everything.

symptom_reasoning.S025: The patient explicitly denies losing interest or pleasure, stating that they still enjoy their normal hobbies and creative activities.

turns.doctor_question: Outside of your art business, do you find yourself worrying a lot about other parts of life too?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. Um, my mind doesn't really do that with other things. I mean, I have normal day-to-day stuff, but I don't find myself worrying a lot about my personal life or anything like that. It really is just... just the business side of my art that's causing all this stress. Everything else is pretty okay.

symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient explicitly denies worrying about multiple domains of life, clarifying that their stress is confined strictly to the business side of their art.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself repeatedly checking or redoing business tasks because you feel you have to, even when you know it’s excessive?
turns.patient_response: No, I don't really do that. I mean, I'll double-check an email before I send it, just normal stuff, but I don't find myself constantly redoing things or checking them over and over. If anything, my problem is that I just avoid starting the business tasks altogether because they stress me out so much. I definitely don't get stuck repeating them.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient explicitly denies engaging in repetitive checking or redoing of tasks beyond normal double-checking.
